answer_1.quote: we propose a novel framework combining question type prediction and eventcentric summarization to generate educational questions for storybooks.

answer_2.quote: For automatic evaluation, similar to , we use the Rouge-L score , and report the average precision, recall, and F1 values. Meanwhile, we also use BERTScore to evaluate the semantic similarity of generated questions with the ground-truth questions, and report the average precision, recall, and F1 values.

answer_3.quote: use BERTScore to evaluate the semantic similarity

answer_4.quote: We conducted a human evaluation with consent of our method against the best-performed baseline QAG (top2). ... After regular group meetings, we concluded the following four dimensions... 1. Question type: whether the generated questions belong to any of the three event types. 2. Validity: whether the generated questions are valid questions according to the original paragraph. 3. Readability: whether the generated questions are coherent and grammatically correct. 4. Children appropriateness: to what extent would you like to ask this question when you read the story to a five year's old child?
answer_4.guideline: Participants rated questions on a five-point Likert-scale for validity, readability, and children appropriateness, and annotated question types.
